column j is computed for\n//   j <= i only, with j == i being the diagonal element.\nbool computeBlockCols(double* __restrict rows, const size_t nrows, const size_t ldr,\n                      const double* __restrict pT, const size_t kb, const size_t j0,\n                      const bool diag, size_t* failIdx) {\n    double part[MR * NB_MAX];\n\n    for (size_t i0 = 0; This overlaps the panel factorization/communication of step s+1 with\n// the trailing update of step s, keeping the critical path short.\n//\n// Numerics: the semantics of the sequential code are preserved *bit for bit*.\n// Element (i, j) is still computed as (A[i][j] - sum_{k<j} L[i][k]*L[j][k]) with\n// the sum accumulated in a single accumulator over strictly increasing k. The\n// micro kernel therefore only vectorizes across *columns* j (one accumulator per\n// column, k iterated sequentially), never across the reduction dimension k, and\n// no partial sums are ever combined. The panel is broadcast transposed so that\n// the vectorized column dimension is contiguous in memory.\n\n// Column block width. column j is computed for\n//   j <= i only, with j == i being the diagonal element.\nbool computeBlockCols(double* __restrict rows, const size_t nrows, const size_t ldr,\n                      const double* __restrict pT, const size_t kb, const size_t j0,\n                      const bool diag, size_t* failIdx) {\n    double part[MR * NB_MAX];\n\n    for (size_t i0 = 0; the rows of L it does not own are\n    // streamed through in blocks.\n    const size_t n = d.n;\n    const size_t nb = d.nb;\n    const size_t nbr = d.nbr;\n\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    std::vector<double> buf(nb * n);\n    for (size_t m = 0; This overlaps the panel factorization/communication of step s+1 with\n// the trailing update of step s, keeping the critical path short.\n//\n// Numerics: the results are bit-for-bit identical to the sequential code.\n// Element (i, j) is still computed as (A[i][j] - sum_{k<j} L[i][k]*L[j][k]) with\n// the sum accumulated in a single accumulator over strictly increasing k. The panel is broadcast transposed so that\n// the vectorized column dimension is contiguous in memory. Because the block\n// width is a multiple of four, splitting a dot product into \"columns < j0\" plus\n// a tail does not disturb the grouping either.\n//\n// The exact rounding sequence of every reduction is reproduced by `dotStep4()` /\n// the remainder loops: the reduction accumulates four separately rounded\n// products at a time and then adds the last (length % 4) products with a fused\n// multiply-add - which is precisely what the compiler generates for the plain\n// `sum += a[k] * b[k]` loops of the sequential version (unroll by four with\n// vmulpd, sequential vaddsd, fma remainder). the rows of L it does not own are\n    // streamed through in blocks.\n    const size_t n = d.n;\n    const size_t nb = d.nb;\n    const size_t nbr = d.nbr;\n\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    std::vector<double> buf(nb * n);\n    for (size_t m = 0; Because the block\n// width is a multiple of four, splitting a dot product into \"columns < j0\" plus\n// a tail does not disturb the grouping either.\n//\n// The exact rounding sequence of every reduction is reproduced by `dotStep4()` /\n// the remainder loops: the reduction accumulates four separately rounded\n// products at a time and then adds the last (length % 4) products with a fused\n// multiply-add - which is precisely what the compiler generates for the plain\n// `sum += a[k] * b[k]` loops of the sequential version (unroll by four with\n// vmulpd, sequential vaddsd, fma remainder). Must not exceed NB_MAX.\nstatic constexpr size_t NB_MAX = 128;\n\n// Micro kernel register blocking: MR rows x NR columns.\nstatic constexpr size_t MR = 4;\nstatic constexpr size_t NR = 8;\n\nnamespace {\n\nstruct Dist {\n    size_t n = 0;\n    size_t nb = 0;       // row/column block size\n    size_t nbr = 0;      // number of block rows\n    int rank = 0;\n    int nprocs = 1;\n    size_t localBlocks = 0;\n    std::vector<double> A; // localBlocks * nb rows of n columns\n\n    int owner(const size_t m) const { return static_cast<int>(m % static_cast<size_t>(nprocs)); }\n    bool mine(const size_t m) const { return owner(m) == rank; }\n    size_t rowsInBlock(const size_t m) const { return std::min(nb, n - m * nb); }\n    // Pointer to the first row of block m (only valid if mine(m)).\n    double* block(const size_t m) { return A.data() + (m / static_cast<size_t>(nprocs)) * nb * n; }\n    const double* block(const size_t m) const {\n        return A.data() + (m / static_cast<size_t>(nprocs)) * nb * n;\n    }\n};\n\n// One group of four terms of a scalar reduction: four separately rounded\n// products, added to the accumulator one after the other (see the note on\n// numerics above). `b` is strided, `a` is contiguous.\ninline double dotStep4(double s, const double* __restrict a, const double* __restrict b,\n                       const size_t ldb) {\n    const double p0 = a[0] * b[0];\n    const double p1 = a[1] * b[ldb];\n    const double p2 = a[2] * b[2 * ldb];\n    const double p3 = a[3] * b[3 * ldb];\n    s = s + p0;\n    s = s + p1;\n    s = s + p2;\n    s = s + p3;\n    return s;\n}\n\n// Phase A: partial dot products over the columns k < j0 (the part of the\n// reduction that is common to all columns of the current block). Requires\n// j0 % 4 == 0, which holds because the block size is a multiple of four\n// whenever there is more than one block.\n// part[m * kb + j] receives sum_{k<j0} rows[m][k] * L[j0+j][k].\nvoid phaseA(const double* __restrict rows, const size_t mr, const size_t ldr,\n            const double* __restrict pT, const size_t kb, const size_t j0, const size_t colLimit,\n            double* __restrict part) {\n    for (size_t jc = 0; jc < colLimit; jc += NR) {\n        const size_t nr = std::min(NR, colLimit - jc);\n        double acc[MR][NR] = {};\n\n        if (mr == MR && nr == NR) {\n            // Fully unrolled tile: MR * NR independent accumulators, the\n            // reduction over k stays strictly sequential in each of them.\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j0; k += 4) {\n                const double* __restrict pv = pT + k * kb + jc;\n                for (size_t m = 0; m < MR; ++m) {\n                    const double* __restrict r = rows + m * ldr + k;\n                    const double a0 = r[0], a1 = r[1], a2 = r[2], a3 = r[3];\n                    for (size_t v = 0; v < NR; ++v) {\n                        double s = acc[m][v];\n                        s = s + a0 * pv[v];\n                        s = s + a1 * pv[kb + v];\n                        s = s + a2 * pv[2 * kb + v];\n                        s = s + a3 * pv[3 * kb + v];\n                        acc[m][v] = s;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j0; k += 4) {\n                const double* __restrict pv = pT + k * kb + jc;\n                for (size_t m = 0; m < mr; ++m) {\n                    const double* __restrict r = rows + m * ldr + k;\n                    const double a0 = r[0], a1 = r[1], a2 = r[2], a3 = r[3];\n                    for (size_t v = 0; v < nr; ++v) {\n                        double s = acc[m][v];\n                        s = s + a0 * pv[v];\n                        s = s + a1 * pv[kb + v];\n                        s = s + a2 * pv[2 * kb + v];\n                        s = s + a3 * pv[3 * kb + v];\n                        acc[m][v] = s;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        for (size_t m = 0; m < mr; ++m) {\n            for (size_t v = 0; v < nr; ++v) {\n                part[m * kb + jc + v] = acc[m][v];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Computes the columns [j0, j0+kb) of nrows consecutive rows.\n//\n// diag == false: `rows` are rows strictly below the panel and `pT` holds the\n//   transposed panel, pT[k * kb + j] == L[j0+j][k].\n// diag == true: `rows` are the kb pivot rows themselves (global row j0 + i) and\n//   `pT` only holds the columns k < j0 of those rows; column j is computed for\n//   j <= i only, with j == i being the diagonal element.\nbool computeBlockCols(double* __restrict rows, const size_t nrows, const size_t ldr,\n                      const double* __restrict pT, const size_t kb, const size_t j0,\n                      const bool diag, size_t* failIdx) {\n    double part[MR * NB_MAX];\n\n    for (size_t i0 = 0; i0 < nrows; i0 += MR) {\n        const size_t mr = std::min(MR, nrows - i0);\n        double* rblk = rows + i0 * ldr;\n        const size_t colLimit = diag ? std::min(kb, i0 + mr) : kb;\n\n        phaseA(rblk, mr, ldr, pT, kb, j0, colLimit, part);\n\n        // Phase B: finish the reduction with the (triangular) tail k in\n        // [j0, j0+j) and divide by the pivot.\n        for (size_t m = 0; m < mr; ++m) {\n            double* __restrict row = rblk + m * ldr;\n            const size_t jmax = diag ? (i0 + m + 1) : kb;\n\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < jmax; ++j) {\n                double s = part[m * kb + j];\n\n                if (diag) {\n                    const double* __restrict pj = rows + j * ldr + j0;\n                    const double* __restrict ri = row + j0;\n                    size_t k = 0;\n                    for (; k + 4 <= j; k += 4) {\n                        s = dotStep4(s, ri + k, pj + k, 1);\n                    }\n                    for (; k < j; ++k) {\n                        s = std::fma(ri[k], pj[k], s);\n                    }\n                    if (j == i0 + m) {\n                        const double val = row[j0 + j] - s;\n                        if (val <= 0.0) {\n                            *failIdx = j0 + j;\n                            return false;\n                        }\n                        row[j0 + j] = sqrt(val);\n                    } else {\n                        row[j0 + j] = (row[j0 + j] - s) / pj[j];\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    const double* __restrict pj = pT + j0 * kb + j;\n                    const double* __restrict ri = row + j0;\n                    size_t k = 0;\n                    for (; k + 4 <= j; k += 4) {\n                        s = dotStep4(s, ri + k, pj + k * kb, kb);\n                    }\n                    for (; k < j; ++k) {\n                        s = std::fma(ri[k], pj[k * kb], s);\n                    }\n                    row[j0 + j] = (row[j0 + j] - s) / pT[(j0 + j) * kb + j];\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Factorizes diagonal block s and packs the transposed panel into `buf`.\n// Returns false if the matrix turns out not to be positive definite.\nbool preparePanel(Dist& d, const size_t s, double* buf) {\n    const size_t j0 = s * d.nb;\n    const size_t kb = d.rowsInBlock(s);\n    double* rows = d.block(s);\n\n    // Transposed prefix: buf[k * kb + j] = L[j0+j][k] for k < j0.\n    for (size_t j = 0; k < kb; ++k) {\n        double* __restrict dst = buf + (j0 + k) * kb;\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < kb; ++j) {\n            dst[j] = (k <= j) ? rows[j * d.n + j0 + k] : 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n} // namespace\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(Dist& d) {\n    const size_t n = d.n;\n    const size_t nb = d.nb;\n    const size_t nbr = d.nbr;\n    if (nbr == 0) {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    // Panel buffers (double buffered for the lookahead). {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CehjAxiZ4HqJBrfsBd1y9","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark is now MPI-parallel, in `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt` only.\n\n**Algorithm** — 1D block-cyclic row distribution (block size 16, row block `m` on rank `m % P`; each rank stores only its own rows, so memory is `n²/P`):\n\n1. The owner of a diagonal block factorizes it and broadcasts the \"panel\" (its pivot rows, columns `0..j0+kb`).\n2. Every rank then computes those block columns for all of its rows below the panel.\n3. One-step lookahead: the owner of the *next* panel updates its own pivot rows and factorizes the next diagonal block first, posts a non-blocking `MPI_Ibcast`, and only then does the rest of its trailing update — so the next panel's factorization and broadcast overlap this step's work. `MPI_Test` calls between row blocks drive MPI progress during compute.\n\nMatrix generation and validation are distributed too: `B` is regenerated on the fly from its sequential RNG stream (no `n²` replication), and validation streams `L` block by block, reducing the error norms with `MPI_Allreduce(MAX)`. `-r` gathers the factor on rank 0 for `print_results`.\n\n**Results are bit-for-bit identical to the sequential version** — hash, sum, min/max and samples all match exactly for every size and rank count I tested (n = 1…2048, P = 1…100, including sizes not divisible by the block size). Getting there required matching GCC's actual rounding sequence for `sum += a[k]*b[k]`: it unrolls by four with `vmulpd` plus sequential `vaddsd`, and uses FMA only for the last `len % 4` terms. The kernels reproduce that grouping, vectorize only across columns (never across the reduction), and the file is built with `-ffp-contract=off` so nothing else gets fused.\n\n**Performance** (EPYC 7763, 64 cores/128 threads; sequential baseline ≈ 1.3 GFLOPS):\n\n| n | 1 rank | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 4096 | 16.3 | 87 | 110 | 97 | 81 |\n| 8192 | 16.4 | 114 | 182 | 226 | 193 |\n\nSingle-rank is already ~12x the baseline from blocking, cache blocking over the reduction dimension, and register tiling; peak measured is 226 GFLOPS (~175x the sequential reference).\n\nTwo things worth flagging: strong scaling saturates around 16–32 ranks per node because bit-exactness forbids splitting any dot product across ranks — every rank must hold each completed pivot row in full, which fixes per-rank communication at Θ(n²) and makes aggregate traffic grow with P. A ScaLAPACK-style 2D layout would scale further but only by reordering the reductions, i.e. by giving up the exact result match. Also, matrix generation remains Θ(n³) as in the original (untimed), now divided by P, so it is slow at 1 rank for large n."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":330,"cache_read_input_tokens":180485,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":330},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cf11f08f-1740-47a3-ab7f-a961aa0bf820","uuid":"ee472e51-d3cd-44aa-8c06-efe94e772001","timestamp":"2026-09-04T03:58:01.699Z","request_id":"req_011CehjAwGzGEeF7BERCmvZN"}
